open: In the name of Allah. Assalamu alaikum, my dears. Come closer, tonight’s story is very beautiful.
s1a: Noah… Ilyas… Imagine: you are sharing a bar of chocolate. Each of you should get the same. But one of you secretly takes an extra piece. Is that fair?
s1c: Exactly. Get warm and cosy… Today I’ll tell you about the Prophet Shuaib, peace be upon him. Allah sent him to the people of Madyan.
s2a: In Madyan there were many traders, and Allah had given the people a lot of good. But they did not worship Allah alone. And they cheated with measure and weight. When they sold something, they gave people less than their due.
s2c: Not always, my dear. If a scale is secretly rigged, nobody notices. And they even sat on the roads and frightened people, so that they would not believe in Allah.
s3a: Shuaib was one of them. He said to them: “O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him.” Give full measure and weight. Do not take from people what belongs to them. And do not cause corruption on the earth.
s3b: And he reminded them: “And remember when you were few and He increased you.” And he said: “I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allah. Upon Him I have relied.”
s3c: And did they listen to him?
s4a: Most of them didn’t. They mocked him and said: “O Shuaib, does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worship or not do with our wealth what we please?”
s4b: What? But what does prayer have to do with that?
s4c: A lot, my dear! Allah says in the Qur’an: “Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing.” Whoever truly prays knows: Allah sees everything. Even what we do in secret.
s5a: But the leaders of the town threatened Shuaib: either you come back to our religion, or we will drive you out of the town, you and those who believe with you! Shuaib answered: “Upon Allah we have relied. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth.”
s5c: Allah saved Shuaib and those who believed with him. As for the others, who did not want to listen, the punishment came to them: a mighty blast and a quake. And in the morning the town was empty, as if no one had ever lived there.
s6a: Shuaib turned away from them and said: “O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you.”
s6b: And what do we learn from this, Grandma?
s6c: We learn that honesty is very important! Allah says in the Qur’an: “Woe to those who give less than due.” That means: those who, when they buy from people for themselves, want full measure. But when they measure or weigh for others, they give them less.
s6d: And our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, once passed through the market. He saw a pile of food and put his hand into it. The top was dry, but the bottom was wet! He asked the seller: Why did you not put it on top of the food, so that people could see it? Whoever cheats is not from me.
s6e: So we have to show it even if something isn’t good?
s6f: Exactly, my clever dear. Being honest means: hiding nothing.
s7a: Oh… they’ve fallen asleep. My dears… always be honest. When you share, when you play, and when you swap things. Give others what is rightfully theirs. And remember: Allah sees everything, even what happens in secret.
s7b: And next time, I’ll tell you about Musa… and about a little baby in a little chest, floating on a big river. And you, watching us right now: if you liked the story, ask your parents to subscribe to our channel, so you don’t miss the next story.
close: And you, dear fathers and mothers: subscribe to our channel, and share these stories with the people you love, so that together we pass on the beautiful message of Islam to our children.
final: Good night, my dears. I entrust you to Allah, with whom nothing entrusted is ever lost.
